newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ debt markets mixed at close after chaotic day.
newsitem.headline: NZ debt markets mixed at close after chaotic day.

text.p: FUTURES PHYSICAL YIELD 90-DAY
OVERNIGHT CASH 10.10 PCT (PREV 10.10) US 30-YR 6.88 (PREV 6.83)
* NZ debt markets end mixed after pre-election juggling
* Mid bonds find support, longs sold in thin trade
* Balance of Payments data fail to inspire
New Zealand debt markets ended mixed in the last trading session before Saturday's general election, which recent political polls suggest will be a nail-biter for financial markets.
The short end found good support while the long end sold during a jittery day one dealer described as an "absolute chaotic mess".

New Zealanders vote on Saturday in the country's first general election under a proportional voting system. Polls suggest a change of government is in store, with the market-preferred conservative ruling National party losing
support to centre-left Labour.
Dealers said some offshore players did not seem to be as concerned as local market participants about the potential repercussions of a centre-left coalition.
They said the 7/98s, 02/00s and 02/01s had held in quite well on the back of buying interest out of Asia, but came back slightly offered at the close.
"They keep buying more. Their theory I suppose is well, look at the inflation rate, look where bond yields are, where else can they put their money and get comparable yields," a dealer said.
"If the economic direction was to change markedly then okay, they might come out big time, but at this point they seem willing to give whoever might get in (to government) the benefit of the doubt."
The long bond climbed 19 points in yield on the day in thin trade to 8.06 percent after encountering selling pressure overnight, while the 02/00s were up eight at 8.05 percent.
Recent eurokiwi and samurai issuing interest had made the mid part of the curve relatively attractive, and dealers said it seemed the safest area given the election uncertainty.
Ninety-day bank bills rallied into the close to shed three points, while the December futures contracts were up two to 90.55.

Traders seemed by and large to have positioned themselves where they wanted to be ahead of the election, dealers said. One said that with the spread between New Zealand and U.S. 10-year bonds widening 13 points to around 150, the market seemed to have priced in a centre-left coalition of some description.
June quarter Balance of Payments data completely failed to inspire the election-focused market, with the deficit coming in only slightly larger than expected.
